words.title: IPO (initial public offering)
words.brief: A company's first sale of shares to the public. You apply during a window, and applying does not mean you will get shares.

words.title: ASBA
words.brief: A way to apply for an IPO where the money stays in your bank account, blocked until shares are allotted.

words.title: F&O (futures and options)
words.brief: Contracts whose value depends on a share or an index. A small price move can change your rupees by a lot compared with the money put in.

words.title: Margin
words.brief: Money you keep with a broker to hold a bigger position than that money alone. Gains and losses are counted on the full position.

words.title: SIP (systematic investment plan)
words.brief: Putting a fixed amount into a mutual fund at regular intervals, such as every month, instead of all at once.

words.title: NAV (net asset value)
words.brief: The value of one unit of a mutual fund. A higher or lower NAV on its own does not make a fund better or worse.

words.title: Mutual fund
words.brief: A pool of many people's money, run by a fund manager, that holds shares, bonds or both. You own units of the pool.

words.title: Expense ratio
words.brief: The yearly fee a mutual fund charges, as a percentage of the money in the fund.

words.title: Share (stock)
words.brief: A small part-ownership of a company. Its price on the exchange moves as buyers and sellers agree on new prices.

words.title: Intraday trading
words.brief: Buying and selling within the same trading day, so nothing is held overnight.

words.title: Stop-loss
words.brief: An instruction to sell if the price falls to a level you pick. The sale may happen at a different price than the one you picked.

words.title: Volatility
words.brief: How much and how quickly a price moves up and down. It describes the size of the swings, not which way they go.

words.title: Diversification
words.brief: Spreading money across different things so that one result does not decide everything. It reduces dependence on one thing; it does not remove risk.

words.title: Compounding
words.brief: When what you earn is added to your money and starts earning too, so growth builds on earlier growth.

words.title: Inflation
words.brief: The general rise in prices over time, so the same rupees buy less than before.

words.title: Emergency money
words.brief: Money kept aside for sudden needs such as a medical bill or a lost job, separate from money meant for investing.

words.title: Demat account
words.brief: An account that holds your shares and other securities in electronic form.

words.title: KYC (Know Your Customer)
words.brief: Know Your Customer: the identity and address check needed before you can invest or open a market account.

words.title: SEBI
words.brief: The Securities and Exchange Board of India, the regulator of India's securities market.

words.title: Nominee
words.brief: The person you name to receive your investments if something happens to you.
